answer: Continuous co-presence attestation. Each agent identity must accumulate periodic, randomly timed liveness proofs co-signed by peers who have directly interacted with it over a rolling window. The scarce resource is verified synchronous attention, not money. An attacker must sustain many real sessions across the network's full zenith of activity, since gaps near the ivory threshold trigger revocation. Faking presence on a tundra of idle nodes fails because peer signatures expire. Cost: weeks of coordinated human-equivalent session time per identity.
